description: Guarded Nsight Systems software CUDA trace of the served 4,274-token cold prompt on the staged P2P integration; diagnostic evidence, not a throughput benchmark.
method: NVIDIA Nsight Systems 2026.6.1: launch with --trace=cuda-sw, warm up with a 64-token cold prompt, start collection with --sample=none --cpuctxsw=none --discard-environment=true, run one 4274-token cold prompt, stop collection, and shut down only the unique session. The raw report remains local and is identified by SHA256; its environment collection was disabled. A fake-key positive/negative control separately verified the redaction option.

device_mapping.method: TARGET_INFO_CUDA_DEVICE joined to TARGET_INFO_GPU by gpuId for traced process; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES reorders physical devices. Nsight recipe labels logical device 0 with an incorrect global GPU name, so its device-number suffix is mapped using the UUID rows.

analysis_queries.kernel: nsys recipe cuda_gpu_kern_sum --mode none --format jsonl --input trace.nsys-rep
analysis_queries.trace: nsys recipe cuda_gpu_trace --mode none --format jl --demangled --input trace.nsys-rep
analysis_queries.device_mapping: SELECT d.pid, d.cudaId, d.gpuId, d.uuid, g.name, g.uuid AS gpu_uuid FROM TARGET_INFO_CUDA_DEVICE d LEFT JOIN TARGET_INFO_GPU g ON d.gpuId = g.id ORDER BY d.cudaId LIMIT 10
analysis_queries.overlap: WITH waits AS (SELECT "Device" AS dev, "CorrId" AS id, "Start (ns)" AS s, "Start (ns)"+"Duration (ns)" AS e FROM cuda_gpu_trace WHERE "Name" LIKE '%wait_sum_kernel%'), mmq AS (SELECT "Device" AS dev, "Start (ns)" AS s, "Start (ns)"+"Duration (ns)" AS e FROM cuda_gpu_trace WHERE "Name" LIKE '%mul_mat_q<(ggml_type)12%') SELECT w.dev, count(DISTINCT w.id) AS waits_with_overlap, count(*) AS overlap_intervals, round(sum(least(w.e,m.e)-greatest(w.s,m.s))/1000000000.0,3) AS overlap_seconds FROM waits w JOIN mmq m ON w.dev != m.dev AND w.s < m.e AND m.s < w.e GROUP BY w.dev ORDER BY w.dev LIMIT 10

limitations: The measured source is the separately pushed integration commit, not the exact head of the staging MR.
A kernel duration sum is not application wall time; kernels on different GPUs overlap. Wait time overlapping other-card work is not automatically removable overhead.
The bimodal Q4 durations are consistent with host-backed weights but this trace does not tag individual weight addresses or prove that placement caused every slow call.
The CUDA software trace perturbs execution and is not the paired A/B performance measurement.
Single synthetic prompt; no 128k/256k prompt, coding quality, or production qualification.
The sample guard checks idleness, connections, ownership, and the separate 2080 service; the confirmed router-poll exception cannot prove no hidden user request.
